Preparation only: no launch, binding, freezing or adoption; the supervisor control file reads pause; no trainer, owner or watcher process runs. Status words: IMPLEMENTED = in a commit or package file; CHECKED = a registered run passed; PROPOSED = designed, not built or not wired.

1. EXACT CHANGED CODE

1a. SOURCE (items 2 and 3 and "Also"). Worktree C:/Users/bhart/Documents/UEMA_wt/s4r_pose_fields_s1_20261022, branch repair/s4r-pose-fields-s1-2026-10-22, HEAD 7dd0eabda (clean), on top of the checked e058c0c81. Changed: causal_chain.py, datasource.py, explainer/schema.py, lem_model.py, observer_model_lane.py, observer_record.py, train_mimo.py, tools/training_preflight.py (the worktree's copy), docs/gain_of_function_v4/probe_planner_candidates.py, and three test files. Commits:
- a0d7eec93, the capture flush connection (item 2). Finding first: --observer-chunk-steps sets the chunk size of both the model lane and the world lanes, but 5 alone does not make a finished capture durable at its boundary. The capture's line is written in after_step, before that model step's lane row is added, and the arrays then travel with the next chunk; the world lane writes only every 5th record. The narrow connection: PlanCapture._save_state calls ModelLane.flush_captures before the line is written (the pending rows and the capture's arrays as one file, written as <name>.part.npz and renamed with os.replace); after the hold's last burst the capture asks every world recorder to write what it holds (datasource observer_flush). No fsync: on disk under its final name survives a process kill, not a power loss.
- 9ad987ef4, --moment-video {on,off}, default on (item 3).
- b6e092bf1, the perturbed alternatives perturb_1/perturb_2 keep the decoder-inert numbers at the plan's own, with the same seeded draws on the live numbers, and every planning record carries alternatives_decoder_inert ("Also"). Old records unchanged.
- c3ea051d2, a world worker that does not answer the flush within 180 s marks the pool out of step; the next src.step then raises (fail closed).
- 7dd0eabda, from the review: the alternatives also hold the eyes' strength (column 8 of the eyes' row: no actuator reads it, the forward model does); and in the model step after a capture's line, ModelLane.write_pending writes the end step's own row right after it is added (train_mimo.py 3365-3371), so the end record is on disk before the next model step.
Review: ACCEPT WITH CHANGES on a0d7eec93..c3ea051d2 (the two changes above), ACCEPT on 7dd0eabda.
CHECKED at 7dd0eabda: decoder_inert_fields_check2 PASS, 27 of 27 tests (pytest 9.34 s); capture_flush_connection_check PASS, 11 of 11 (3.52 s); video_switches_check PASS, 7 of 7 (2.61 s). Configuration delta of a2: --observer-chunk-steps 5 added, --video-every-min 20.0 -> 0, --moment-video off added. Image files still written in a2: a live frame every model step (--live-view-every 1) and the observer's left-eye audit images every 10 minutes.

1b. COMPLETION READER (item 1). Repair package D:/UEMA_Research/external/D/UEMA_scratch/h84/d1_planner_recovery/s4r_pose_learning_496250_repair_package, read_pose_learning.py sha256 8a0a231c... (from 74c21047 through 32f442b5; both kept in versions/). IMPLEMENTED: a FINAL reading reads every observer lane file whole (numpy.load, every member read; names ending .part.npz never read) and PASSes only when every counted plan capture's arrays, its model rows (plan, +1, end) and its world records (start, +1, end, goal) are on disk and join to the line: the meta, the shapes, the command bit for bit (SHA-256 of the sent and executed rows), the column maxima, the wrist rows, the goal-pose validity, the cm and pose-error readings, the latch flag and the command sequence counter (code name order_seq), and the new lane_flush/world_flush records. Otherwise exit 3, verdict INVALID, never FAIL, with the cause named in invalid_reasons: detail records missing or not joined; a renamed causal_chain_*.jsonl beside the capture file (its lines would not be counted); a line whose body count differs from --bodies; capture-line write failures above 0, or their counts unreadable, in any stats record after the start step. A health failure still exits 2 (FAIL) and takes precedence. Missing detail never enters the failures list; every reading stays in the output and the usable outcomes with joined detail are listed apart as the valid partial results; no checkpoint is read. A LIVE reading keeps exit 0 or 2 only. Historical a1 files are neither re-read nor rewritten. Reviews: ACCEPT WITH CHANGES on 32f442b5, ACCEPT on 8a0a231c.

1c. OWNER. Logic b986ff6e -> da57ffb0 (versions/; generator make_owner_exit3.py): READER_INVALID_EXIT = 3; aggregate_blocks labels a final reading's exit 3 "INVALID: ..."; run_reader no longer calls it a crash; owner_verdict(blocks) gives INVALID when every block is the reader's INVALID and FAIL beside any other block; owner_end.json gains measurement.verdict. The training row's own verdict (arm_end.json) and the preserved checkpoint are untouched by the reading. The reading row reads the reader's "verdict" key, so exit 3 reads INVALID in the registry. Path step d2e8c84c... (wiring only). Review: ACCEPT. CHECKED by the durability check's owner conditions (below). Real code: the lanes and the capture writer at 7dd0eabda, the reader 8a0a231c run whole, the owner's functions from da57ffb0. One synthetic run (2 bodies, model steps 1000 to 1036, captures at plan steps 1005 and 1020) written in the trainer's sequence of calls; the lanes never closed. Shown: both captures' arrays and every row and world record they name read whole before any shutdown, the reader exits 0 (PASS) and the owner's verification reads both durable; a truncated copy under a final name is rejected as unreadable by both, a leftover .part.npz is never read, and the reader exits 3 (INVALID) with the detail records as the only cause, on each of the two damaged copies; the owner turns exit 3 alone into INVALID and exit 3 beside a training failure or an INCOMPLETE block into FAIL, keeps exit 2's text and verdict, and gives PASS for exit 0. Not shown: the trainer's own wiring of the calls (checked by capture_flush_connection_check's source checks), the world flush across worker processes, real world records, a power loss, damage other than truncation, a2's sizes, a live reading, the reader's other INVALID causes.

2. MEASURED GEOMETRY GAPS (item 4). Tests row arm_geometry_readback_check PASS (program v2 400c9e57..., reviewed READY; 1.289 s). Scope as authorized: the 51 saved tenure records of S4R_measure_496000 on code d6a12e317, the body head's lesson-route forecasts of EXECUTED commands, authors planner (the sensory trust_v2 search) 25, reflex_noise 17, reflex 7; 49 records joinable, 392 record-body pairs, each read for the left and the right arm. Not the launched search; shoulder and wrist limits not tested; feasibility not judged. Every number is the forecast F composed by forecast_pose's rule, against C, the same composition of the measured change (the noise floor); 0 = the link kept exactly.
- Identity: C reproduces the measured end E within storage-derived bounds on all 29,400 position and 9,800 turn elements (largest 0.9996 and 0.985 of the bound); the measured-reference error on the arm and chest handles is at most 0.0045 cm and 0.0147 degrees.
- Shoulder link residual (the upper arm's origin against its place on the chest): left median 0.205 cm, 90th percentile 0.429, max 0.869; right 0.214, 0.397, 0.883; C's maximum 0.0012 and 0.0009 cm. All 392 forecasts per side are above C's maximum.
- Upper-arm link residual (the elbow against the upper arm's length and direction): left median 0.811 cm, 90th percentile 1.598, max 4.456; right 0.733, 1.591, 3.987; C's maximum 0.0037 and 0.0031 cm; 392 of 392 above.
- Elbow off-axis turn (a pure hinge turn reads 0): left median 3.43 degrees, 90th percentile 8.31, max 31.6; right 4.76, 11.3, 27.7; C's maximum 0.019 and 0.022 degrees; 392 of 392 above.
- Elbow angle beyond the scene's range: left 4 of 392 pairs (max 7.57 degrees), right 12 of 392 (max 12.7).
- Forearm-to-hand distance outside its recorded range: left 241 of 392, right 325 of 392. The recorded range on this run's poses (11.43 to 12.33 cm left, 11.99 to 12.32 cm right) is narrower than the wrist ranges allow (the hand's origin moves with the hand's turn), so outside the recorded range is not outside the legal range.
- Floor: the forecast left hand's origin below the floor plane in 2 of 392 pairs (max 0.22 cm); body origins only.
- Against the forecast's own movement: the median shoulder-link residual is 0.61 (left) and 0.59 (right) of the upper arm's forecast movement; the median upper-arm-link residual 0.81 and 0.61 of the forearm's.
Reading: on these records every forecast places the chest, upper arm and forearm so that no rigid arm joins them, by a residual that is a large share of the forecast movement, while the same composition of the measured change keeps every link to within 0.004 cm. The launched search's per-handle forecasts were never saved; a2 records them (forecast_pose__iteration0_* and __selected_*).

3. IK/FK (joint-limited fit with forward-kinematics rebuild). Branch repair/s4r-arm-ik-fk-2026-10-22, worktree C:/Users/bhart/Documents/UEMA_wt/s4r_arm_ik_fk_20261022, commits 7e584f83a, 6df694078, d79c9c114, c86363ae2 (HEAD, clean, from e058c0c81): Source/Python/mimo_bridge/arm_pose_fit.py (882 lines), tests/test_arm_pose_fit.py (15 tests), docs/gain_of_function_v4/agents/arm_forecast_fk_fit_2026-10-22.md. Four independent reviews: ACCEPT WITH CHANGES three times, ACCEPT on c86363ae2. Status: IMPLEMENTED in the branch and imported only by its test file; NOT CHECKED (no test run: 12 of the 15 need MuJoCo and the saved world model); NOT WIRED.
IMPLEMENTED BEHAVIOUR. Input per body: the forecast poses, positions [26, 3] world cm and quaternions [26, 4] x y z w. Per arm: (1) the forecast chest and arm parts are moved rigidly onto a scratch chest at the compiled model's reference pose (distances and turns kept); (2) the arm's 7 hinges (3 shoulder, elbow, 3 wrist) are fitted inside their ranges by the existing reach-projection code (_Arm.project: the decoder's stacked arm solve, flow at 0.3 of each solved change, at most 400 iterations or until no hinge is asked to turn more than 1e-9 rad, then an L-BFGS-B polish inside the ranges) with targets on all three arm parts (position at 8 rad per metre and orientation, strength 1, no reach clip); (3) mj_kinematics rebuilds the fitted arm, carried back onto the forecast chest; (4) per part, the position residual (cm) and rotation residual (degrees). Output: the forecast rows unchanged, the fitted angles, the hinges resting on a stop, the rebuilt pose, the residuals, the solver readings and a status: fitted_within_tolerance (every part at or under its lines), fitted_residual_above_tolerance (only after a second fixed start also ends above), fitted_tolerance_uncalibrated (no calibration record), or fit_failed with a reason (bad input, solver fault). Nothing is written into the forecast, a score or a command. The tolerances are None until a calibration record passes its declared pass line: at least 100 poses per arm with every hinge inside its range, the poses rounded to float32 as the live forecast is, every floor fit started from the recorded angles and stationary, angle recovery within 1e-3 rad, no fit failure, the locality fits run, and the arm geometry fingerprint the lines were measured on.
WHY THE SELECTED FORECAST'S PARTS CAN FAIL TO SHARE ONE LEGAL ARM (IMPLEMENTED in today's code; the readback measures it on executed commands): the body head reads each handle's 6 move-and-turn numbers out of one shared 256-unit vector, separately per handle (efference.py 632-649, layers 469-472); to_lived scales them (708-719); forecast_pose composes each handle on its own (physical_goal.py 104-110); the lesson grades each handle against its own measured change (efference.py 1189-1197); the search and the selection compare per-handle forecast errors only. No link length, hinge axis, range, shoulder attachment, floor or contact enters any of these steps.
WHAT CHANGED COMPUTATION WOULD PREVENT ACCEPTANCE (PROPOSED, not wired): in IntentionGenerator.generate_action, after each evaluation, fit that evaluation's forecast; a candidate whose fit fails or exceeds a line is not eligible at the selection (pose_primary_improved, line 551); the first command is eligible only when its forecast passes the fit and predicts progress against the measured start; a changed command must pass the fit and beat both the measured start and the iteration-0 forecast; the fitted pose never enters the score, the loss or the recorded forecast; the record keeps failed fits apart from forecasts above their lines.
ALL-POSE FAILURE (PROPOSED): an iteration-0 forecast that fails the fit stops the decision; no eligible choice for a body stops the whole 8-body batch in-process before src.step, with a matching model-and-world save and no rejected command executed. None of this exists today: save_ckpt writes the worlds only at an episode boundary, which is False between the decision and src.step, and the control.json poll every 25 model steps cannot stop the failing decision's own command. The five pieces such a stop needs are written down, not built (your review conditions say not to build them now). An exception inside the search takes the crash path (model checkpoint without the worlds; no command of that decision is sent).
WHAT THE LINES WOULD COST A GATE (ARITHMETIC, from the lines' own premise): a line is the largest of n floor residuals, so a consistent forecast exceeds it with chance 1/(n+1); a decision checks 96 lines (8 bodies x 2 arms x 3 parts x position and rotation). With n = 100, a decision of consistent forecasts stops with chance 7.7 of 100 if each body's 12 exceedances come together, 61.5 if all 96 are independent, 63.6 if a body's never coincide; with n = 1,000, 0.8 to 9.1. Holding it at or under 1 in 100 decisions takes n of 796 to 9,557. The one measured sample of the proposed progress rule: on a1's 6 captured decisions it stops 1 (model step 496,310, body 3: the first command forecast an error of 4.6516383 against the measured start's 3.2466377, and no changed command beat both), before any geometry test.
COMPUTATIONAL COST (ARITHMETIC on the reused solver's measured 71.6 ms median and 121.2 ms 90th percentile for both arms of one body, Sept 25, 960 commands): every forecast of one decision (8 bodies x 21 evaluations = 168 fits) in one process, 12.0 s; in the 8 world processes, at least 2.55 s (the trainer waits for the slowest of 8); fitting only candidates that would become the best, 1.15 to 12.0 s. At one decision per 5 model steps against 2.0 s per model step (Sept 25), the arithmetic training rate is 45, at most 80, and at most 90 of 100. Work bounds per arm and start: the flow at most 400 iterations; the polish at most 6,000 potential evaluations (scipy's defaults); a second start doubles both. The fit's own time on 250 ms forecasts is unmeasured.
MOTOR AND CONTACT LIMITS: within tolerance means one arm shape exists, never that the body reaches it in 250 ms (Sept 25 paired physics: the arms closed 49 to 66 of every 100 degrees of a reachable goal in 250 ms; arm motors on their rail in 77.6 of 100 records); no torque, weight or contact check; poses held past a soft limit go to a separate allowance.

- The geometry gate: PROPOSED only. Missing: the arm-fit tests' first run, the tolerance calibration, the choice of an acceptable stop rate (it sets n), arm geometry and measured arm hinge angles in the learner process, and the stop-before-src.step machinery with its matching save.
- The reaching defects: preflight gates 4, 5 and 7 still read FAIL.

5. EXECUTABLE NEXT ACTIONS (each needs your decision)
- A. Bind, freeze and launch a2 as prepared: one block of at most 100 model steps from the preserved complete 496,250, which writes the launched search's first durable per-handle forecasts (iteration 0 and selected) and the joint states.
- B. One registered run of the 15 arm-fit tests (CPU, MuJoCo with the saved world model, no training).
- C. One registered tolerance calibration on recorded poses with their hinge angles.
- D. After A: the fit readback of a2's iteration-0 forecasts, which measures the per-body failure share of the proposed gate.

DECISIONS NEEDED
1. --moment-video: main's preflight checker (the launch's) treats it as a configuration flag, so a2's fingerprint is 83ff9dd7eb5e2699 as prepared; adding the source branch's RUN_FLAGS line to main makes it 4b8a769eec7f699e, needs one rebuild of the package chain, and lets a later change of only that switch keep the record. Neither choice changes a gate verdict.
2. The geometry decision for a2: launch as prepared (no geometry gate; it records the forecasts), or wait for B and C.
3. For any later gate: the stop rate you accept on consistent forecasts.
4. Whether to authorize B and C.
